column1: # Verified written sources — engineering blogs, conference proceedings, practitioner sites.
# Columns: url <TAB> name <TAB> reach <TAB> what it is good for
# WHY WRITING RANKS ABOVE VIDEO. An essay is QUOTABLE and a talk mostly is not: YouTube captions
# mishear proper nouns even on tracks YouTube labels "manual" (references/public-sources.md). So when
# a claim has to survive into a plan or a review as a quote, prefer the written source — and several
# of the people in references/practitioners.tsv publish the same idea in both places.
# THE REACH COLUMN IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. `fetch` = a plain HTTP GET returns 200. `browser` = the
# host bot-blocks a plain fetch (403/406) and needs a real browser — Netflix's blog, OpenAI's
# research index and Uber's engineering blog all do. That distinction matters because a 403 read as
# "nothing there" silently removes a source from consideration, which is the same failure as never
# HOW TO READ ONE: `WebFetch` for a known page; `WebSearch` to find the page when you lack the URL.
# For a `browser` row, drive whatever browser-automation tool the environment provides. NEVER mint a
# credential or automate a login to reach a source (compound-v:agent-security) — if the only way
# through is someone's session and you do not have it, the honest output is "this channel is closed
# THE BAR IS THE SAME ONE THE CHANNELS USE: the person who did the thing, in their own words,
# non-obvious, and load-bearing. A corporate engineering blog carries both real mechanism and
# recruiting content under one domain, so the row says which half to read for.

column4: Agent harness design, context engineering, effective agents. The primary source for most of what this kit encodes about agents.
The best free writing on distributed-systems mechanism anywhere: timeouts, retries, backoff, constant work, idempotency. Written by principal engineers who operate it.
The canonical scoping of YAGNI, sacrificial architecture, and refactoring. Read for the distinctions, which are sharper than any restatement.
Peer-reviewed systems papers and SRE practice. Where a claim about production behaviour can actually be checked.
Architecture talks with written transcripts — quotable in a way YouTube captions are not.
The conference behind the densest YouTube channel on this list; the site carries schedules and speaker material.
Frontier research write-ups. Read for mechanism, not product.
Unusually candid postmortems and networking/edge mechanism. The outage write-ups are the valuable half.
Repo-scale engineering, Actions, Copilot internals.
Infrastructure at scale. Skip the hiring posts.
Money-movement correctness — idempotency, reconciliation, API versioning. This is where Stripe's real material is; their YouTube channel is brand content.
Next.js/React and AI SDK engineering from the maintainers.
Security research with working exploits. The bar for what a real vulnerability write-up looks like.
Harness engineering for coding agents, including public reversals of their own earlier advice — rare and valuable.
Long-form interviews with engineers at named companies. Some posts paywalled.
The most consistent running commentary on LLM tooling, with working code and honest negative results.
Engineering leadership and architecture decisions from a repeat CTO. Strong on how a decision gets made, not just what it was.
Measured, contrarian systems writing. Frequently the only source that checked a widely-repeated claim.
Idempotency keys, job queues, Postgres patterns — implementation-level and unusually precise.
Resilience engineering and incident analysis; the strongest writing on why systems fail as systems.
Debugging and systems fundamentals explained from first principles. Best source for "how do I actually inspect this".
Large-scale streaming and platform engineering. Medium bot-blocks a plain fetch (403).
Model and agent research index. Bot-blocks a plain fetch (403).
Distributed systems and data infrastructure at scale. Bot-blocks a plain fetch (406).

Full written transcripts of the interviews registered in channels.tsv (DwarkeshPatel), plain-fetchable at /p/<slug>: a curl of /p/andrej-karpathy returns ~154k chars with "march of nines" verbatim and proper nouns intact ("Claude Code" x3, "Cloud Code" x0 — the test that demoted captions). This is the quotable form of a talk that is otherwise ASR. Slug is the guest name (/p/john-schulman, /p/jeff-dean-and-noam-shazeer, /p/sholto-trenton-2); /sitemap.xml lists every slug. Fetch serially — eight parallel requests returned 17-char rate-limit bodies that read as empty pages. 2021-era episodes (/p/uncle-bob) have no transcript body.

The eval methodology most AI teams now run, in its authors' words: error analysis before metrics, judge context scoping, trace sampling, reviewing a trace too large for a person. The AI Evals FAQ (/blog/posts/evals-faq/) answers the specific question. 14 sources.md rows cite the site. They sell a course; read the posts and the FAQ, not the course pages.

First-person agent-design writing from Flask's creator, now building agents at Earendil: what breaks in harnesses, why a sub-LLM inside a tool backfires, a cache-friendly prompt shape, iteration isolated in throwaway sub-agents. 5 sources.md rows cite it. His company's engineering posts are at earendil.com — same orbit.

cognition.ai/blog redirects here; 23 sources.md rows cite it. Read the bylined engineering and research posts — Walden Yan on multi-agents and its later revision, Ido Pesok on verifying agentic development, SWE-grep, FrontierCode's move from pass/fail to mergeability grading, the Devin annual performance review — and skip the launches. A company measuring its own agent is mechanism, never measurement.

Bylined engineering posts from a team operating a high-usage agent: harness iteration across model releases, a semantic-search A/B, dynamic context discovery, agent-swarm economics, reward hacking swamping benchmark gains (Wilson Lin, Stefan Heule, Jediah Katz, Naman Jain). Mixed with Composer and product launches; vendor figures are mechanism, never measurement.

Context failure modes ('How Contexts Fail'), prompt debt, keeping spec, tests and code in sync — with his own reversals ('I got this wrong') and small tools that test the claims. Several posts relay papers or system cards; follow those to the primary before citing. DSPy/cmpnd commercial orbit, shared with lateinteraction.
